subject: Unexpected A/B quality regression — orchestration & temporary fallback
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Ballard <sarah.ballard@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected A/B quality regression — orchestration & temporary fallback

Team —

Quick heads-up: AtlasHealth (see Sarah on cc) reported a spike in low-quality outputs in the new A/B bucket that started yesterday evening. Early signal: answer-coherence drop from 96% -> 86% on our internal metric and a correlated uptick in safety flags for hallucinations on certain clinical prompts. I pulled the attached regression_log_20280411.csv and a short sample of failed items (failed_examples_abridged.pdf).

Asking for a coordinated triage and a temporary orchestration plan:
- Product: confirm whether this A/B included prompt template changes or model variant swaps (Aditya)
- Applied ML: quick hypothesis sweep (quantization/VE/temperature) and a mitigation you can ship within a day (Stephanie)
- QA/Ops: validate the metric and produce a minimal repro set and prioritization (Naomi)

My immediate recommendation is to enable the fallback routing policy for this cohort (route to last-known-good model variant + deterministic post-filter) and pause any further rollout for AtlasHealth only while we triage. If we agree, I can ask infra to deploy the routing override for the AtlasHealth customer id.

Next steps I need in 2 hours:
1) Naomi: confirm acceptance criteria we would use to clear this (what delta on coherence + safety is acceptable)
2) Stephanie: short triage plan and the quickest mitigation you can test (reranking threshold / deterministic answer patch / revert to earlier prompt set)
3) Sarah: please confirm you want us to pause the rollout to AtlasHealth while we investigate (we'll keep the rest of customers unaffected).

Thanks —
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachments: regression_log_20280411.csv (text/csv), failed_examples_abridged.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Ballard <sarah.ballard@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected A/B quality regression — orchestration & temporary fallback

Thanks Aditya — I started looking at the CSV. Quick notes:
- The metric definitions used in the graph are coherence_score (ensemble of n-gram overlap + human-labeled sanity for a small sample) and the safety_flag boolean from our safety classifier.
- The drop looks concentrated on prompts in the "med-summarize" family where the A/B included a prompt-change that shortened the instruction pacing.

Can you confirm which commit moved the prompt template and whether the A/B used a different model compile (quantization/8-bit) for cost reasons? If so that would be priority #1 for me.

Acceptance criteria proposal (I can formalize):
- Coherence_score delta <= 2 pct absolute vs control on the med-summarize sample (n=500)
- Safety_flag rate not to exceed control by >1 pct absolute

I'll prepare a reproducible sample (subset of 100 prompts + expected outputs) and upload to the runbook link shortly.

- Naomi
QA Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected A/B quality regression — orchestration & temporary fallback

I'm on it. Initial hypotheses and actions I can run in parallel: 
1) Prompt template truncation -> increase instruction verbosity (quick A/B of +1 token)
2) Model variant mismatch / compile differences -> roll sampled requests through the last-known-good execution path (same kernels, same quantization flags)
3) Sampling/temperature change unintentionally introduced -> enforce deterministic decoding + constrained top-k/top-p for the cohort

Practical mitigation I can test and stage in the next 3 hours:
- Deploy a temporary routing override: route AtlasHealth bucket to model-v2.3-stable (known-good) and add a reranking filter with lower hallucination tolerance. This requires infra signoff but is low-risk and reversible.

If Naomi confirms acceptance criteria, I can run a small controlled re-eval (n=200) against the production shard and report back within 3 hours. I also created a short checklist in the runbook link for triage steps.

- Stephanie
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Thanks both — I agree with the routing override. Steph, please proceed with the temporary routing change for AtlasHealth only. Naomi, please share the repro sample and validation script to the runbook page.

I'll open a short-lived escalation ticket with infra to ensure we can toggle the override within 15 minutes of a rollback decision. Sarah — we will pause the rollout to AtlasHealth immediately after the override is live; we won't affect other customers. Apologies for the disruption — we want to be conservative here.

Action owners I have:
- Stephanie: deploy routing override -> model-v2.3-stable + reranker (ETA 3 hours)
- Naomi: upload repro set and final acceptance criteria (ETA 2 hours)
- Aditya: coordinate infra ticket and messaging to AtlasHealth (ETA 30m)

I'll follow up with infra ticket id when it's open.

Aditya
